entry.title: Who is the likeliest to seize power by 2035: frontier lab, a national government, or a small group?

link.title: Who is the likeliest to seize power by 2035: frontier lab, a national government, or a small group?

entry.content:
Contents

  1. Where does this question come from?
  2. Discussion
    • 2.1 Current state
    • 2.2 Frontier lab or national government?
    • 2.3 A small group?
  3. Conclusion
  4. References

1. Where does this question come from?

As costs increase dramatically, including the cost of chips and of talented researchers, the development of AI requires more and more resources and money [1]. This is analogous to a normal business war in a specific industry. If AI is actually just a normal technology [2], I believe it will end up the same way: a few frontier AI labs will take control of most of the AI market, including the development of AI. But the crucial difference is that AI is generally considered more than a normal technology. People are concerned that AI will not only bring convenience and financial influence across the world, but will also affect how much power one can seek [3].

In the past, every technology wave caused a panic: people were scared of being replaced or fired by their firms [4]. One wave similar to AI is the internet. When the internet came out, the middle of the job market shrank. Meanwhile, demand for high-skill and low-skill workers actually grew [5]. Some people argue that AI will end with the same result. This can be challenged by the fact that past technologies could “only” increase the efficiency of workers, not replace the workers themselves. To illustrate, in past technology waves a worker was always needed, whether the original workers were kept or replaced by higher-skilled or lower-skilled workers. However, in the AI wave, it is now possible to simply cut the worker and use AI instead [6]. This is not only about unemployment; it is worth noting that a person who uses AI could do everything by himself with AI. This is where the “one-person company” comes from [7]: one person can hold all the power in the company, because the company’s performance no longer depends on team members, but only on that person and the AIs, which are in some sense equivalent to the person himself.

This leads to today’s question: will a certain group of people be able to use AI to seize power? Will it be the frontier labs, the national governments, or a small group?

2. Discussion

2.1 Current state

In current AI development, there is a big gap between industry and academic research. 91% of notable AI models come from industry, while only 2% come from academia [8]. This can be explained by another comparison: 80% of AI supercomputer capacity is owned by companies, not by research institutions or governments [9]. All of this information points to the complete lead of the frontier AI labs. Will this situation be maintained until 2035?

2.2 Frontier lab or national government?

One of the biggest problems for an ideal one-person company is trust. In the past, when performance was not ideal, we could argue that one of the team members (components) was holding the team back, and that person would take responsibility. However, when it comes to your AI worker, even if you suspect that the AI worker is not as satisfactory as before, you cannot do anything about the provider. Even if the provider has not actually lowered its performance, you will still doubt it, because the AI is a black box [10] and you have no sense of control over these AI bots, whereas you are able to “control” and “trust” your workers through salary and the threat of unemployment.

There is a similar trust issue between governments and frontier AI labs. Nowadays, there is no doubt that national governments hold most of the power. They control the military, and they are responsible for political events and all the big decisions. When AI develops so fast that it can make significant contributions to governments, will governments believe that frontier AI labs are giving them the best models? This is the trust problem: they will never believe it unless they know the complete details of all the frontier labs.

Can the frontier labs fight back? It will not happen unless there is a significant change, with something other than AI emerging, because all of these models rely on chips and the internet. They are all based on hardware [11]. If so, the national government, which controls the military, will always have the right to make the final decision on the frontier labs’ fate. This leads to the result that the frontier labs are the least likely to maintain their leading position and seize power, and they will in some way become part of the national government [12].

It is worth considering a very special scenario in which the frontier labs also have military power [13], even though it would definitely be highly restricted by the government. They might have autonomous robot systems that do not need human soldiers to cooperate [3]. This might change the distribution of military power all over the world, causing complete confusion in AI development, and even in world development.

2.3 A small group?

Since we suggest that national governments will lead most AI development, it is worth discussing whether a small group of people (inside the government) will take charge of it. It seems that AI has recently become able to help train AI [14]. Will this develop until AI can train better AI without human assistance [15]? In that case, will the people who hold the latest models and have access to the supercomputer capacity take over all frontier AI development? They would be the only ones in charge of training AI. This would be extremely dangerous if they could train AI according to their own preferences without others’ supervision [3]. It would be even more alarming if such people came from the national government. If a person controls both frontier AI and military power, he could become so powerful that he cannot be restrained. This would definitely be harmful to human development overall.

Therefore, such small-group control of development should be prevented, and more people from different sides and fields should be brought in and involved, so they can oversee each other and form a balance.

3. Conclusion

I would suggest that national governments will maintain their positions and seize more power than the frontier labs. A small group of AI “leaders” should not be permitted, and more people should be involved here.

References

  1. Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2025, Chapter 1: Research and Development (2025). Rising training costs, e.g. about $170M for Llama 3.1-405B.
  2. Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor, “AI as Normal Technology”, Knight First Amendment Institute (April 2025).
  3. Tom Davidson, Lukas Finnveden and Rose Hadshar, “AI-Enabled Coups: How a Small Group Could Use AI to Seize Power”, Forethought (April 2025).
  4. Jeremy Rifkin, The End of Work (1995). An example of past fears of technological unemployment.
  5. David Autor and David Dorn, “The Growth of Low-Skill Service Jobs and the Polarization of the US Labor Market”, American Economic Review 103(5) (2013).
  6. Jan Kulveit et al., “Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development” (January 2025).
  7. Paolo Confino, “Could AI create a one-person unicorn? Sam Altman thinks so”, Fortune (February 2024).
  8. Stanford HAI, AI Index Report 2026, Chapter 1: Research and Development (2026). Industry produced 93 of 102 notable models in 2025; academia alone produced 2.
  9. Konstantin Pilz et al., “Trends in AI Supercomputers”, Epoch AI (April 2025). Companies’ share of AI supercomputer performance rose from about 40% (2019) to 80% (2025).
  10. Teun van der Weij et al., “AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations” (2024).
  11. Girish Sastry et al., “Computing Power and the Governance of Artificial Intelligence” (February 2024).
  12. Leopold Aschenbrenner, Situational Awareness, “IV. The Project” (June 2024).
  13. Mikayla Easley, “Pentagon awards mega contracts to Musk-owned company, other firms for new ‘frontier AI’ projects”, DefenseScoop (July 2025). Contracts worth up to $200M each to Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and xAI.
  14. Google DeepMind, “AlphaEvolve: A Gemini-powered coding agent for designing advanced algorithms” (May 2025). It cut Gemini’s training time by about 1%.
  15. Daniel Kokotajlo et al., AI 2027 (April 2025). A scenario in which AI automates AI research.
entry.summary: On frontier AI labs, national governments, small-group control, and the case for shared oversight by 2035.

entry.title: Should AI speech be limited?
entry.content:
How AI speech is defined can affect the discussion. I believe it should be defined broadly as AI-generated content that performs a communicative function. The AI speech can be concluded into three categories: The model-led-speech is generated by the model itself, such as the initial responsible in a conversation; The human-led-speech is led mainly by users, such as content for which users employ AI to turn their ideas into the ideal AI speech. The mixed-speech is a mix of users’ ideas and model’s contribution. While they often coexists in a chat, it is worth discussing them separately.

The model-led-speech shouldn’t be limited beyond the safeguards had already imposed on the mode. To be specific, this content mainly comes from its training rather than clear guidance from the users. The argument that model-led-speech should be limited can be formed:

  1. Nobody is responsible for these instances of AI speech

  2. If such speech causes harm, nobody is going to take the moral responsibility

  3. So we should limit these AI speech.

Premises 1 and 2 can be revealed through the evident question – psychological harm – The model might mislead and harm the users when it attempts to give psychological help, including the personalized persuasion, instead of only providing objective advice. For instance, the AI might make commitments like physical affection or love, that only actual humans can fulfill, during the conversation. Some may argue that humans may do the same, but the difference is the human takes the moral responsibility for their speech while no one appears to be responsible for AI speech in this case. It is supported by Millican’s argument against attributing consciousness to machines, so that they don’t have the intention to deceive the users. Some argue that the AI itself is responsible. But it also fails, as it still doesn’t explain how an AI system could bear moral responsibility. If we trace back the development of AI, we find that many people involved in the training process, the one deciding the training method, the one selecting data used… Moreover, the contemporary AI training is more likely to be a “black-box” rather than a clear and transparent procedure. It functions as an integrated whole that you cannot break the outputs down to components. Another response is that the response could be a matter of chance. AI is probabilistic model that would output the most “probable” answers. Nowadays, even with the same setup, the same model, and the same settings, AI could generate different, even opposite answers. So the producers of AI couldn’t actually take the moral responsibility of the model-led AI speech, if the model is checked and permitted. However, the conclusion doesn’t lead to the limitations. Because premise 2 will only be valid under the assumption that the user always takes the AI speech as truth. This only reveals that we shouldn’t take AI as a human and expect it to take the moral responsibility of their speech, we should instead consider it as a powerful and convenient source of information. In “A Theory of freedom of expression”, Scanlon argues that the state should respect listeners as capable of deciding what to believe. In a similar way, when we are dealing with the freedom of AI speech, we should respect users as capable of deciding which AI speech to believe and how AI speech is used. I suggest that the users could take the moral responsibility if they aim for the acknowledgement of the AI speech. For the “know” here, It would be suitable to use the counterfactual account of knowledge:

You knows “the AI speech” if and only if

  1. “the AI speech” is true

  2. You believed in “the AI speech”

  3. If “the AI speech” is not true then you won’t believe it.

In this way, the model-led speech will be beneficial, and it thereby undermines premise 2, as the users will be the one that takes the moral responsibility here. So the conclusion 3 fails, there aren’t enough reasons to support the limitation of model-led-speech.

The human-led-speech is the category that should be limited. It is different from the former: as the speech were used to express users’ ideas and showed their intentions. I believ that the users directing the speech should take the moral responsibility for the influence of this AI speech. As we just discussed, AI shouldn’t be attributed any specific intention, only the users and AI involved in the speech, the relevant communicative intention comes from the uses . It could be considered as the users’ speech. While AI lowers the barriers for people to present ideal speech, it may also increase the influence of evil. There are several real-world cases: the hackers used AI to hack a church website and obtain the personal details of people registered in the site. They defraud people of their money using this information. The consequences extend beyond fraud. The church, as an example, would have to spend more money to build up the firewall defending the hackers, this increases the cost of building a website and running a beneficial organization, because you will have to spend more time to maintain and protect your site. This is extra work influenced by AI. Last but not least, the development of video-generated AI is also a double-edged sword — the digital version of you can be created easier and more vivid using your information. It will be harder to clarify, if evil tries to use the image or video to default people. This creates an additional need for verification. As the human-led-speech benefits the creation, it is worth recognizing the risk that coexists with those benefits . I suggest the human-led-speech should be limited. The limitation is more straightforward as some people need to take moral responsibility. To protect privacy, we should clarify the AI speech, before identifying identity before risky approaches, such as the video generated based on real humans and prohibit dangerous use, such as the malicious codes for the evils.

The third kind of AI speech, the mixed-speech, is a common case when you are discussing new topics with AI. At first glance, its classification may seem ambiguous that both sides contribute to the speech. However, I argue that it is a mistake to treat it as a distinct category. It should be included in human-led-speech. Some may argue that these prompts may be influenced by AI. But this fails, as if we follow the idea of model-led-speech, the users will know the AI response and then give a new prompt. In this perspective, humans are always leading the speech.

In conclusion, I suggest the freedom of AI speech, based on Scanlon’s argument, and I propose that we should not treat AI speech as human speech because AI itself lacks moral responsibility. I recategorize the three kinds of speech, and clarify that the mixed speech are included in the human-led speech. Finally, I suggest we shouldn’t limit the model-led speech under the assumption that the AI model has been tested and judges reasonably safe and users should be expected to evaluate and know the AI speech, and the necessity to limit the human-led speech by identification and stricter controls, because AI speech can a,plify human intentions.
entry.summary: On human-directed and model-led speech, moral responsibility, and what should justify restrictions on AI-generated communication.

entry.title: Competition
entry.content:
Should we obtain direct competition?

In philosophy, there’s several schools that doesn’t support competition. For example, in daoism, daoists suggest wu wei (无为) . Some questioned that if direct competition will always lead to a failure at some point, why don’t we avoid the competition? Some may argue that, it is coward to quit competition directly. However, we can instead add regulations to the competition we attend. Take me as an example, I used to be only in the competition of computer science, however I change the competing environment by changing major to computer science and philosophy. There’s least participants in this competition. So it should be easier for you to get a higher rank in the new competition.

It is natural to follow up that can we keep doing this? Like adding philosophy to computer science, can we then add football, calligraphy… to form a new competition? It seems that you can! and intuitively you will get a even higher rank in this competition. Can we keep doing this infinitely?
entry.summary: A short reflection on competition, changing its terms, and the comparisons we choose to make.

entry.title: First-person view and third-person view – From determinism

link.title: First-person view and third-person view – From determinism

entry.content:
What is determinsim?

Determinism is formally defined as: For any time t, the complete state of the world at time t together with laws of nature logically entails the complete state of the world at any later time.

And it is stated by the philosopher Peter Van Inwagen that people couldn’t have done any steps given the assumption that determinsim is true:

  • We are discussing about a people A doing action B.
  • We are using the complete state of the world at time T0, which is before the birth of A, we referred it to P0. And now when we refer to the complete state of the world when A’s doing action B as P, we can logically entails P by P0 and the law of nature, by the definition of determinism.
  • Consider the scenario that people A instead doesn’t do action B but any other action C. In this case, it is an observable change in the complete state of the world, so the state can no longer be P, it is the people A (or action C) renders P false. However, while one cannot render the law of nature false, one can also cannot affect the world at the moment that he doesn’t even exist at time T0, so they form a contradiction that the conjunction of two true statement leads to (entails) a false statement. So it is stated that people couldn’t have done anything other than the action they actually did.

It leads to the version of determinism that is easier to understand: Every action of people’s act is determined (completely fixed) by all the past events and law of nature.

The idea of different perspectives of view from determinism

From determinism, we can infer that every action we did is fixed. So our whole life routine is also fixed, as we can break it down to every actions you would, and will do – and they are all fixed. We can analogues our life to a film, which also has a one and only plot. The difference between this film and the film in the traditional sense is that you are the one and only main character.

It is also given by determinism, we can freely do whatever we want, while this action is both determined, and it won’t affect the (one and only) plot. Consider the scenario we literally do nothing, the film will still goes on, we are actually becoming the audience of the film. This won’t affect the film. It is the film that once it starts, nothing will stops it or changes it until it ends. I would rather call this audience-view as the third-person view, and the main-character-view as the first-person view. You are observing your life, how your life goes on, or how does the film goes on as the third person: even though you know the person you observing is actually you, but nothing you do will ever change anything, so you are free and welcome to become an audience, you can even assume that you are watching a person’s life, a film, that is not relevant to you. All of this action is acceptable, by determinism.

Intuitively, you can somehow always maintain the first-person view, while it’s not a wise idea to always maintain the third-person view. So we need to and can switch between them. (While it is also straightforward that the action of switching between perspectives is also acceptable under the determinsim assumption) To illustrate, the way we switch depends on if you switch to third perspective on purpose.

  1. If you are switched to the third-person without purpose, which is frequent when your subconcious mind realize that you can’t bear the strong emotion you are experience while you haven’t realized yourself – (The switch to the third-person view) This is a protection by the subconcious mind. While there’re other scenarios that might lead to the switch without your will, the switch-back normally take place when you experience a complete change in the state. For example, in the case we just mention, when you have overcome or deal with the emotions successfully, you can switch back to the first-person view. Notice that the swicth-back can possibly take place without notice.
  2. If you are switched to the third-person view with purpose. You notice that you are going to switch back at some moment, this should be some boundaries set by you. I would classified them into two kinds, either after a period of time , or when one specific condition is reached. While It is similar to the for loop and while loop in computer science, I suppose the latter is more natural, we are seeking for a sign that we would like to switch back to the first-person view again.

Why we need this the concepts and how do we use them

I believe the third-person view do make a difference when dealing with specific scenarios.

As what I just mention, you can act like and is actually watching a movie of a person who may doesn’t related to you at all in a third person view. This can bring us to the most naive and ideal state: It can be analogued to the state the artists and calligraphers pursue – the child state – you are observing and discovering yourself with the pure interest on a person. In order to try to overcome self-ego, using third-person view to learn yourself from the start should be attempted.

From another point of view, it can also help you adjust your instant emotions. I would try to use the third-person view when I feel nervous and I would rather not, as the negative feelings might somehow affect my perfomances. Switching to third-person view give me a sense of peace, and when I switch back to myself, I would have better state to face the upcoming challenge. For me, it is like a cheatsheet, I would definitely use first-person view to expreience the extreme happiness and joy, and use the third-person view to try to avoid the extreme negative feelings. Even though all of this is corresponding to each other, I believe I make myself the most comfort through my control on myself.
entry.summary: Thinking through determinism and the practical difference between first-person and third-person perspectives.

entry.title: Self-discipline and pleasure – From Hedonism
entry.content:
What are we living for?

This is a basic and general question for all human-beings. It is hedonism that suppose that: The fundamental motivation for a person to do something is pleasure.

Moreover, it is also discoverable that some pleasure are more desirable the others – there’s not only quantity difference but also quality difference on pleasure. This is refered to high pleasure doctrine, that there are some pleasure are better than other independently of quantity.

I agree with high pleasure doctrine, so in one way we can discuss the pleasure you get by both considering the quality and quantity, multiplication of these two seems to be the most straightforward and reasonable way to visualize it. I believe in this perspective, we are living for obtain the maximum pleasure we can get in our life.
entry.summary: A short note on hedonism, the quality of pleasure, and what self-discipline might aim at.
